COORDINATION

Plan a lighting handover before installation starts

A handover works better when its documents and responsibilities are agreed while the package is being scoped.

Define the deliverables in the project scope

The client, consultant and contract determine the final handover requirements. The following are planning topics to agree, rather than a universal statutory checklist.

  • Required inspection and test records
  • As-built drawing ownership and revision process
  • Equipment schedules and manufacturer information
  • Operating and maintenance information
  • Outstanding-item review and acceptance responsibilities

Keep the installed asset identifiable

Consistent asset references make it easier to connect a pole, circuit or panel with its drawing and maintenance record. Agree the identification system and document conventions with the project team. Do not wait until the end to decide which records are needed.

Include the practical maintenance interfaces

Discuss access to elevated luminaires, isolation arrangements, equipment clearances and the responsibilities for replacement parts. A complete document pack does not resolve an installation that cannot be accessed safely for its intended maintenance.

Make the boundary between parties explicit

Use the quotation or a scope matrix to identify who supplies equipment, performs installation, arranges inspections and prepares each record. Where another contractor provides civil works or supply connections, record the interface and the information they must hand over.

This is independent project-planning guidance. It does not replace your project specification, professional design or current authority requirements.
